passages.title: Koʻk velosiped
passages.text: Bobur yozgi taʼtilda bozorda ishladi. U har kuni ertalab amakisiga meva sotishda yordam berardi. Har shanba amakisi unga ozgina pul berardi. Bobur bu pulni sarflamadi, hammasini kichik qutichaga yigʻib bordi. Avgust oxirida qutichadagi pul velosipedga yetdi. Bobur doʻkonda velosipedni oʻzi tanladi: koʻk rangli, oldida savatchasi bor velosiped. Onasi: «Oʻz mehnating bilan olgan narsang yanada qadrli boʻladi», dedi. Endi Bobur maktabga piyoda emas, velosipedda boradi va ertalab vaqti koʻproq qoladi.
passages.author: agent:k5-reading

passages.title: Tandirdagi non
passages.text: Shanba kuni Madina buvisiga non yopishda yordam berdi. Buvisi xamirni bir kun oldin, kechqurun qorib qoʻygan edi. Madina zuvalalarni yoydi va ustiga sedana sepdi. Birinchi non biroz kuyib qoldi. Buvisi kulib: «Tandir hali juda qizib turibdi, biroz kutamiz», dedi. Ular bir piyoladan choy ichib olishdi. Keyingi nonlar qizgʻish va chiroyli chiqdi. Issiq nonlarning ikkitasini Madina qoʻshnilarga olib chiqdi.
passages.author: agent:k5-reading

passages.title: Yoʻqolgan mushukcha
passages.text: Sardorning Paxmoq degan kichkina mushukchasi bor. Bir kuni kechqurun Paxmoq uyda koʻrinmadi. Sardor singlisi Laylo bilan hovlini, bogʻni va koʻchani qidirib chiqdi, lekin mushukcha topilmadi. Sardor juda xafa boʻldi. Keyin dadasi mashinani qoʻyish uchun garajga kirdi va Sardorni chaqirdi. Paxmoq garajdagi eski kiyimlar solingan qutida shirin uxlab yotgan ekan. Dadasi kulib: «Bundan keyin garaj eshigini yopib yuramiz», dedi.
passages.author: agent:k5-reading

passages.title: Kutubxona kitobi
passages.text: Nilufar maktab kutubxonasidan qushlar haqidagi katta, rangli kitobni olgan edi. Kechqurun u kitobni varaqlab oʻtirganida choy toʻla piyolani turtib yubordi. Kitobning oxirgi sahifalari hoʻl boʻlib, bir-biriga yopishib qoldi. Nilufar tun boʻyi yaxshi uxlay olmadi. Ertalab dugonasi: «Hech kim sezmaydi, javonga qoʻyib qoʻyaver», dedi. Ammo Nilufar kitobni toʻgʻri kutubxonachiga olib bordi va boʻlgan voqeani aytib berdi. Kutubxonachi sahifalarni birma-bir koʻzdan kechirdi va: «Rostini aytganing uchun rahmat. Sahifalar qurisa, oʻqisa boʻladi», dedi. Keyin u Nilufardan shanba kuni yangi kitoblarga yorliq yopishtirishga yordam berishni soʻradi. Shanba kuni Nilufar dugonasini ham ergashtirib keldi.
passages.author: agent:k5-reading

passages.title: Jasurning oʻrigi
passages.text: Bahorda mahalla yoshlari koʻcha boʻyiga oʻn ikkita oʻrik niholi oʻtqazishdi. Ariqdagi suv nihollarning hammasiga yetib borardi, faqat burchakdagi oxirgi nihol balandroq joyda edi. Bir oydan keyin uning barglari sargʻayib, osilib qoldi. Koʻpchilik «Bu nihol tutmaydi» dedi. Hatto uning oʻrniga yangi nihol oʻtqazishni taklif qilganlar ham boʻldi. Jasur esa har kuni kechqurun uydan chelakda suv tashib, nihol tagiga quydi. Doʻstlari futbolga chaqirganda ham u avval nihol tagiga suv quyib, keyin borardi. Kuzga kelib, burchakdagi nihol boshqalaridan qolishmaydigan darajada koʻkarib ketdi. Qoʻshnilar uni hazillashib «Jasurning oʻrigi» deb atay boshlashdi. Jasur bu gapni eshitib, faqat jilmayib qoʻydi.
passages.author: agent:k5-reading

passages.title: Avtobusdagi sumka
passages.text: Akmal har kuni maktabga avtobusda qatnaydi. Bir kuni u oxirgi bekatda tushayotganda oʻrindiqda qolib ketgan qora sumkani koʻrdi. Sumka ichida kitoblar, koʻzoynak va kichik daftar bor edi. Daftarning birinchi sahifasida ism va telefon raqami yozilgan edi. Akmal sumkani haydovchiga bermoqchi boʻldi, lekin haydovchi xoʻrsinib: «Bunday narsalarning koʻpi egasiga qaytmay qoladi», dedi. Shunda Akmal sumkani olib maktabga keldi va oʻqituvchisining telefonidan daftardagi raqamga qoʻngʻiroq qildi. Kechqurun sumka egasi — keksa bir oʻqituvchi ayol — maktabga keldi. U koʻzoynagisiz kitob oʻqiy olmasligini, ertaga esa ertalabki darsi borligini aytdi va Akmalga qayta-qayta rahmat aytdi.
passages.author: agent:k5-reading

passages.title: Ipak qanday olinadi
passages.text: Ipak — tut ipak qurtining pillasidan olinadigan tola. Ipak qurti faqat tut bargi bilan oziqlanadi, shuning uchun ipakchilik qilinadigan joylarda tut daraxtlari koʻp ekiladi. Qurt yetarlicha oʻsgach, atrofini ingichka ip bilan oʻrab, pilla yasaydi. Pilla bir necha boʻlak ipdan emas, bitta uzun, uzluksiz ipdan iborat: uning uzunligi bir necha yuz metrga yetadi. Bu ip yopishqoq modda bilan birikib turadi. Shuning uchun pillalar issiq suvga solinadi: issiq suv yopishqoq moddani yumshatadi va ipni sidirib olish oson boʻladi. Ammo bitta pilla ipi juda ingichka. Shu sababli bir necha pilla ipi birlashtirilib, mustahkamroq ip hosil qilinadi va undan mato toʻqiladi.

facts.claim: Silkworm larvae eat only mulberry leaves.
A cocoon is one thread of raw silk about 300 to 900 m long.
Cocoons are put in hot water, which frees the filaments (sericin removed) for reeling.
Single filaments are combined to form thread.

passages.title: Loy
passages.text: Kulol Hamid aka shogird olganida, Sanjar birinchi kundanoq lagan va kosalarga naqsh chizishni orzu qilardi. Ammo usta unga moʻyqalam emas, belkurak tutqazdi. Uch oy davomida Sanjar faqat loy tayyorladi: uni suvda ivitdi, elakdan oʻtkazdi, ichidagi havo chiqib ketguncha uzoq ezgʻiladi. Baʼzan u ichida «Usta meni shunchaki qora ishchi qilib oldimi?» deb oʻylardi. Bir kuni usta tokchadan chiroyli naqshli, lekin yorilib ketgan kosani olib, Sanjarga uzatdi. «Buni yoshligimda yasaganman, — dedi u. — Naqshi hali ham koʻzni quvontiradi, ammo loyni shoshib tayyorlagandim. Pishirganda ichidagi havo pufakchasi kosani yorib yubordi.» Sanjar kosani qoʻlida uzoq aylantirib, jim qarab turdi. Ertasi kuni u loyni avvalgidan ham sinchiklab, shoshmasdan tayyorlay boshladi. Usta buni koʻrib, hech narsa demadi, faqat kechqurun Sanjarning ish joyiga yangi moʻyqalamlar qoʻyib ketdi.
passages.author: agent:k5-reading

passages.title: Ulugʻbek rasadxonasi
passages.text: Samarqanddagi rasadxona 1420-yillarda Mirzo Ulugʻbek tashabbusi bilan qurilgan. Uning asosiy asbobi radiusi qariyb qirq metr boʻlgan ulkan sekstant edi; u oʻz davridagi eng katta astronomik asbob hisoblangan. Asbobning kattaligi osmon jismlarining holatini juda aniq oʻlchash imkonini bergan. Biroq bunday ulkan asbobni toʻliq yer ustida qurish uchun bino haddan tashqari baland boʻlishi kerak edi va u qulab tushishi mumkin edi. Shu sababli quruvchilar asbobning bir qismini yer ostiga, ariqsimon chuqurlikka joylashtirishgan. Rasadxonada olib borilgan kuzatishlar asosida taxminan ming yulduzni oʻz ichiga olgan katalog — «Ziji Sultoniy» tuzildi. 1449-yilda Ulugʻbek oʻldirilgach, rasadxona vayron qilindi, olimlar esa shaharni tark etishga majbur boʻlishdi. Rasadxonaning oʻrni asrlar davomida unutildi va faqat 1908-yilda arxeolog Vasiliy Vyatkin uning qoldiqlarini topdi. Bugun undan faqat poydevor va asbobning yer ostidagi qismi saqlanib qolgan.

source.licence: text is our own; only facts are taken, each checked against the cited page

facts.claim: Built in the 1420s in Samarkand by Ulugh Beg.
Main instrument: the Fakhri sextant, radius 40.04 m, the largest astronomical instrument of its time.
Part of the sextant was built underground in a ditch, because a building tall enough could have fallen in on itself.
The Zij-i Sultani listed around 1,000 stars.
After Ulugh Beg's assassination (around 1449) the observatory was destroyed and astronomers were driven away.
Vassily Vyatkin uncovered the remains in 1908; today only the foundations and the buried part of the instrument are visible.

passages.author: agent:k5-reading

passages.title: Orol dengizi
passages.text: Orol dengizi bir vaqtlar dunyodagi eng katta koʻllardan biri edi. Uning hech qanday oqib chiqadigan joyi yoʻq: dengiz suvni faqat bugʻlanish orqali yoʻqotadi. Uzoq vaqt bu yoʻqotishni ikki daryo — janubdan Amudaryo va sharqdan Sirdaryo keltirgan suv qoplab turgan. 1960-yillarning boshida bu daryolar suvining katta qismi choʻllarni, birinchi navbatda paxta dalalarini sugʻorishga burib yuborildi. Endi dengizga kelayotgan suv bugʻlanib ketayotgan suvdan ancha kam edi. Natijada dengiz yildan-yilga sayozlashdi va bir necha alohida koʻlga boʻlinib ketdi. Suv kamaygani sari undagi tuz miqdori oshdi, mahalliy baliqlarning koʻp turlari yashay olmay qoldi va baliqchilik deyarli toʻxtadi. Suv chekingan joyda tuz va kimyoviy moddalar bilan qoplangan tekisliklar paydo boʻldi; shamol ularni uzoq-uzoqlarga uchirib ketadi. Orol voqeasi bir qarorning oqibatlari butun bir hududning tabiati va odamlar hayotiga qanchalik keng tarqalishi mumkinligini koʻrsatadi.

source.licence: text is our own; only facts are taken, each checked against the cited page

facts.claim: The Aral Sea was formerly one of the largest lakes in the world (third or fourth largest by area).
It is an endorheic lake: no outflow, water is lost by evaporation.
It was fed by the Amu Darya from the south and the Syr Darya from the east.
In the early 1960s the rivers were diverted to irrigate the desert, mainly for cotton.
The shrinking sea split into separate lakes; salinity rose and native fish species died out; commercial fishing collapsed.
The exposed seabed left plains covered with salt and toxic chemicals that the wind carries far.

passages.title: Первый снеговик
passages.text: В субботу выпал первый снег. Маша и её младший брат Тимур сразу выбежали во двор лепить снеговика. Снег был мокрый и хорошо лепился. Они скатали три кома: большой, средний и маленький. Для глаз Тимур принёс два чёрных камешка, а для рук — две ветки. Морковки дома не оказалось, поэтому нос сделали из красного перца, который дала соседка. К вечеру пошёл дождь. Утром от снеговика остались только камешки, ветки и красный перец.
passages.author: agent:k5-reading

passages.title: Новая ученица
passages.text: В класс пришла новая ученица, Алина. Она переехала из другого города и никого здесь не знала. На первом уроке Алина открыла пенал и поняла, что забыла ручки дома. Она покраснела и тихо сидела, не зная, что делать. Её сосед по парте, Дима, молча положил перед ней свою запасную ручку. На перемене он показал Алине, где находятся столовая и библиотека. Через неделю они уже вместе ходили домой: оказалось, что они живут в соседних домах.
passages.author: agent:k5-reading

passages.title: Ключ
passages.text: Артём пришёл из школы и не нашёл в рюкзаке ключ от квартиры. Родители были на работе до шести часов. Артём сел на ступеньки и расстроился. Тут открылась дверь напротив, и соседка, Вера Павловна, пригласила его к себе. Она напоила его чаем и предложила сыграть в шахматы. Артём играть не умел, но за два часа узнал, как ходят все фигуры. Когда мама вернулась, ключ нашёлся: он лежал в кармане куртки, которую Артём утром не надел.
passages.author: agent:k5-reading

passages.title: Пауза
passages.text: Лена целую неделю учила стихотворение для школьного концерта. Дома она читала его без единой ошибки, но перед выходом на сцену у неё вдруг задрожали руки. На середине второго куплета она замолчала: следующая строчка будто исчезла из головы. Зал притих. И тут из-за кулис послышался шёпот её подруги Кати, которая держала в руках листок с текстом. Лена услышала первые слова, улыбнулась и спокойно дочитала до конца. После концерта несколько ребят сказали ей, что пауза показалась им специальной — будто Лена хотела подчеркнуть важную мысль. Лена только переглянулась с Катей. Вечером она написала в дневнике: «Хорошо, когда рядом есть человек с листком».
passages.author: agent:k5-reading

passages.title: Одна большая кнопка
passages.text: Бабушка Кирилла много лет пользовалась кнопочным телефоном и не хотела его менять. На день рождения родители подарили ей смартфон. Бабушка поблагодарила, но положила коробку в шкаф. Через месяц Кирилл заметил, что коробка так и не открыта. Он не стал уговаривать бабушку, а просто спросил, чего ей не хватает в старом телефоне. Оказалось, бабушке очень хотелось видеть внуков, которые живут в другом городе, а не только слышать их голоса. В тот же вечер Кирилл настроил смартфон и сделал на экране одну большую кнопку — видеозвонок двоюродной сестре. Теперь бабушка каждое воскресенье звонит сама, а старый телефон лежит в ящике «на всякий случай».
passages.author: agent:k5-reading

passages.title: Бумажная карта
passages.text: Класс Саши отправился в однодневный поход в горы. Учитель заранее попросил взять бумажную карту, хотя у всех были телефоны с навигатором. Ребята посмеялись: зачем карта, если есть телефон? Днём небо затянуло тучами, пошёл дождь, и группа спряталась под скалой. Когда дождь кончился, оказалось, что тропинку размыло, а связи в ущелье нет. Навигаторы показывали только серый экран. Учитель развернул карту, нашёл на ней ручей и сказал, что вдоль него можно спуститься к дороге. Через час группа вышла к автобусу. На обратном пути Саша спросил, можно ли ему взять карту домой, — «чтобы научиться её читать».
passages.author: agent:k5-reading

passages.title: Почему осенью желтеют листья
passages.text: Летом листья зелёные из-за хлорофилла — вещества, с помощью которого растение поглощает энергию солнечного света. Хлорофилла в листе так много, что он скрывает другие пигменты. В конце лета дни становятся короче, а погода — холоднее. Дерево готовится к зиме: хлорофилл в листьях разрушается, а часть полезных веществ растение забирает из листьев обратно. Когда зелёный цвет исчезает, становятся видны жёлтые и оранжевые пигменты — каротиноиды. Они были в листе всё лето, просто их не было видно. Красный цвет появляется иначе. У некоторых деревьев красные пигменты, антоцианы, образуются в листьях только к концу лета и осенью, и чем ярче в это время свет, тем их больше.

facts.claim: Chlorophyll lets plants absorb energy from light and makes them look green.
Shorter days and cooler temperatures in late summer start leaf senescence; the plant recovers nutrients from the leaves; chlorophyll is broken down.
Carotenoids (yellow-orange) are present all year but masked by chlorophyll.
Anthocyanins are not present all season but are produced towards the end of summer; brighter light gives more anthocyanins.

passages.title: Второе место
passages.text: Дина три месяца готовила рисунок для городского конкурса. Она выбрала непростую тему — старый рынок рано утром, когда торговцы только раскладывают товар. Первое место получила работа с яркими красками и закатом над морем; Дине дали второе. Вечером она хотела порвать свой рисунок, но мама попросила подождать до утра. На следующий день Дине позвонил один из членов жюри, пожилой художник. Он признался, что до последнего спорил за её работу: «Закат нарисовать нетрудно — он красив сам по себе. А вы сумели сделать интересными ящики с луком и мокрый асфальт». Он предложил Дине по субботам приходить к нему в мастерскую. Дина положила трубку и долго смотрела на рисунок. Порвать его ей больше не хотелось; наоборот, она впервые заметила в нём места, которые можно сделать лучше.
passages.author: agent:k5-reading

passages.title: Почему в горах трудно сварить картошку
passages.text: Многие думают, что вода всегда кипит при 100 °C. На самом деле это верно только при обычном атмосферном давлении — таком, как на уровне моря. Температура кипения зависит от давления воздуха над жидкостью: чем оно ниже, тем при меньшей температуре вода закипает. В горах воздух разрежён и давление меньше, поэтому вода закипает раньше, чем внизу. Например, на высоте около 1900 метров вода кипит примерно при 93 °C, а на вершине Эвереста — около 71 °C. Кипящая вода в горах бурлит так же, как и внизу, но она холоднее. Поэтому продукты, которые варят в воде, например картофель или макароны, готовятся дольше, а при очень низкой температуре кипения могут так и не свариться. В высокогорье поэтому часто пользуются скороваркой: в плотно закрытой кастрюле давление выше, и вода в ней закипает при более высокой температуре.

facts.claim: Water boils at 100 °C under standard pressure at sea level; the boiling point depends on surrounding pressure.
Water boils at about 93.4 °C at 1,905 m and about 71 °C on Mount Everest.
At high altitude lower air pressure lowers the boiling point; food takes longer to cook or may not cook; pressure cookers are used to compensate.

passages.title: Что на самом деле хранит горб верблюда
passages.text: Долгое время многие считали, что верблюд хранит в горбу воду. Это не так: горб состоит в основном из жировой ткани. Жир — это запас энергии, и животное расходует его, когда корма мало. Вода же хранится не в горбу, а в организме, прежде всего в крови. При этом верблюды действительно поразительно выносливы. Одногорбый верблюд, дромедар, может потерять из-за обезвоживания до 30 % массы тела, тогда как большинство млекопитающих погибает уже при потере 12–14 %. А добравшись до воды, верблюд способен выпить за один раз до 140 литров. Получается, что горб и умение долго обходиться без воды — это две разные особенности, которые люди долго считали одной. Горб помогает пережить голод, а с жаждой верблюд справляется благодаря тому, как устроен весь его организм.

facts.claim: Camel humps are reservoirs of fatty tissue, a reserve of calories, not water.
A dromedary can lose up to 30% of its body mass to dehydration; most mammals withstand only 12-14%.
A camel can drink up to about 140 litres at a time; the water is held in the bloodstream.

passages.title: The Yellow Umbrella
passages.text: On Monday morning, Leo saw dark clouds and took his yellow umbrella to school. By lunchtime the sky was blue, so he left the umbrella in the classroom. After school it began to rain again. Leo was already halfway home when he remembered the umbrella. He ran back, but the classroom was locked. A girl from his class, Sara, was waiting for her father at the gate. She shared her big umbrella with Leo, and her father drove them both home. The next day Leo brought Sara a bag of apples from his grandmother's garden.

passages.title: Saturday Pancakes
passages.text: Every Saturday, Nadia's family has pancakes for breakfast. This Saturday, Nadia wanted to make them herself. She mixed flour, eggs, milk and a little sugar. Her first pancake was too thick and stayed raw in the middle. Her older brother said, "Use less batter, and wait until the pan is hot." Nadia tried again. The second pancake was thin and golden. By nine o'clock there was a tall stack on the table. Her parents said they were the best pancakes of the year, and her brother asked her to teach him the recipe.

passages.title: Park Gate
passages.text: Omar's family moved to a new flat in September. Now Omar takes the number 12 bus to school. On the first day he got off one stop too early and had to walk for fifteen minutes. He arrived just as the bell rang. That evening he wrote the name of the right stop on a small card: "Park Gate." He put the card in his pocket. The next morning he looked at it twice on the bus, and he got off at the right place. After a week he did not need the card anymore.

passages.title: Twenty-Four Pictures
passages.text: Hana's uncle lent her his old film camera for the school photo project. "You get only twenty-four pictures," he warned, "so think before you press the button." At first Hana found this annoying. With her phone she usually took ten photos of the same thing and kept the best one. Now she walked around the neighbourhood for an hour before taking her first picture: a man feeding pigeons by the fountain. She waited until the birds rose into the air. When the film was developed a week later, only eighteen photos were good, but her teacher chose the pigeon picture for the school wall. Hana returned the camera with a thank-you note. At the end she wrote: "Next time, I will take fewer photos and look longer."

passages.title: The Ice Test
passages.text: For the science fair, Kamal and Rosa wanted to find out which material keeps ice from melting the longest. They put an ice cube of the same size in each of four cups: one wrapped in foil, one in wool, one in newspaper and one with no cover at all. They checked every ten minutes and wrote down what they saw. Rosa was sure the foil would win because it looked "cold." To their surprise, the ice in the wool lasted the longest. Their teacher explained that wool traps air, and trapped air slows down the movement of heat. "But wool keeps us warm," Kamal said. "Exactly," the teacher answered. "It slows heat in both directions."

passages.title: Grandpa's Notebook
passages.text: When Grandpa broke his leg in May, Tom promised to look after his vegetable garden. Grandpa gave him a notebook with instructions: water the tomatoes in the evening, not at noon; pull weeds after rain, when the soil is soft; never step on the beds. For the first two weeks Tom watered at noon, because it was easier for him after lunch. The leaves began to look tired, and some turned brown at the edges. Tom read the notebook again and changed his routine. By July the plants were taller than he was. When Grandpa finally walked into the garden with his stick, he did not say much. He just picked a tomato, ate it, and handed Tom the notebook. "Keep it," he said. "Next year you'll write the instructions."

passages.title: The Dance of the Honeybee
passages.text: When a honeybee finds a good patch of flowers, she returns to the hive and tells the other bees where it is by dancing. Inside the hive it is dark, and the bees dance on the vertical surface of the honeycomb. In the waggle dance, the bee runs in a straight line while shaking her body from side to side, then circles back and repeats the run. The direction of the straight run carries the message. A run straight up the comb means "fly towards the sun." A run tilted to the right of straight up means "fly at that same angle to the right of the sun." The length of the waggle carries the distance: the farther away the flowers, the longer the waggle lasts. For flowers very close to the hive, bees use a different, simpler movement called the round dance.

facts.claim: An upward waggle run on the vertical comb means the food is in line with the sun; angles left or right of up code angles left or right of the sun.
Distance is coded by the duration of the waggle run: the farther the target, the longer the waggle phase.
For nearby food (about 10 m) honeybees perform the round dance instead.
Cavity-nesting bees dance in the dark on a vertical plane, using gravity for orientation.

passages.title: Page Two
passages.text: Aziz had spent two weekends on his essay about the river near his village, and he was proud of every sentence. He asked his cousin Malika, who studied literature, to read it, half expecting praise. She returned it covered in pencil marks. "Your first paragraph describes the river for half a page," she wrote, "but I only start caring on page two, when your grandfather teaches you to swim. Begin there." Aziz felt the heat rise in his face. He put the essay in a drawer and told himself that she had not understood what he was trying to do. Three days later he took it out, meaning to prove her wrong, and read it as if a stranger had written it. Halfway through the first paragraph he noticed that he was skimming. He crossed out the opening, moved the swimming lesson to the top and cut the essay by a third. When he sent the new version to Malika, he added one line: "You were right about page two, but I'm keeping the sentence about the willow trees." She replied with a single word: "Fair."

passages.title: What the Moon's Phases Are Not
passages.text: Many people believe that the Moon's phases are caused by Earth's shadow falling across it. The explanation sounds reasonable, but it is wrong. At almost every moment, the Sun lights up one half of the Moon, just as it lights up the half of Earth where it is day. What changes over the month is how much of that sunlit half we can see from Earth. When the Moon lies roughly between Earth and the Sun, its lit side faces away from us, and we see a new moon: almost nothing at all. As the Moon moves along its orbit, we see more and more of the lit half, until, when it is on the far side of Earth from the Sun, we see the whole lit face: a full moon. Then the process runs in reverse. A complete cycle of phases takes about 29.5 days. Earth's shadow does sometimes reach the Moon, but that event has a different name, a lunar eclipse, and it can happen only at full moon.

facts.claim: Phases are not caused by Earth's shadow; they are caused by the Moon's shadow on itself, as Earth's shadow makes night.
When the Sun and Moon are on the same side of Earth the Moon is new and its Earth-facing side is unlit.
A lunar month (same phase to same phase) averages about 29.5 days.
Lunar eclipses happen only during a full moon, when the Moon passes through Earth's shadow.

passages.title: Why Steel Ships Float
passages.text: A solid block of steel dropped into the sea sinks at once, yet ships made of steel carry enormous loads across oceans. The explanation goes back to a principle described by Archimedes more than two thousand years ago: an object in a fluid is pushed upward by a force equal to the weight of the fluid it pushes aside. A small steel block pushes aside only a little water, far less than its own weight, so it sinks. Shape the same steel into a wide, hollow hull full of air, and it pushes aside a large volume of water before it is fully under. The ship settles until the water it has pushed aside weighs exactly as much as the ship itself, and there it floats. The same principle explains a rule that sailors follow. Fresh water is slightly less dense than seawater, so a ship must push aside more of it to balance the same weight. That is why a loaded ship floats deeper in a river than at sea, and why the load marks painted on its side include a separate line for fresh water.

facts.claim: Archimedes' principle: the buoyant force equals the weight of the fluid displaced; formulated by Archimedes around 246 BC.
A steel ship floats because it encloses air, so its average density is less than water's.
A floating object displaces fluid equal to its own weight.
Ships float deeper in fresh water than in seawater; load lines include fresh-water marks for this reason.
